title: Phase isolation scheduler: isolate prefill and decode phases to reduce tail latency and improve fairness
creator: Asha Raman
description: Motivation: Current mixed prefill/decode scheduling causes high tail latency for short decode-heavy requests and starvation for large prefill-heavy requests under bursty load. We want a policy that isolates phase resource windows (phase isolation) so prefill work and decode work do not contend unpredictably for GPU kernels and KV cache bandwidth. This ticket proposes an experimental scheduler policy that: 1) assigns short time-sliced phase windows to groups of requests based on phase dominance (prefill-dominant vs decode-dominant), 2) enforces soft caps per window to guarantee minimum throughput for each phase, and 3) integrates with kernel-selection hints and attention-path priorities so expensive attention kernels are scheduled in prefill windows while low-latency decode kernels are prioritized in decode windows. Goals: reduce 95/99th percentile latency for decode-dominant requests by >= 20% under mixed workloads; reduce starvation incidents for long prefill requests by >= 50%; keep end-to-end throughput within 5% of baseline and not increase average latency for steady-state traffic. This ticket covers design, simulation, small-scale experiment rollout, and metrics collection. The design must document interaction with KV cache eviction, batching windows, and kernel selection heuristics. It also needs tests to ensure no correctness regressions across model families (causal vs. encoder-decoder).
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler implements configurable phase windows (ms granularity) and per-window soft caps
Integration points for kernel-selection hints are implemented (scheduler can tag batches with kernel preference)
Automated simulation shows decode P99 latency improvement >= 20% for our mixed synthetic workload (50% short decode, 50% long prefill)
No increase >5% in steady-state throughput measured on perf harness for at least three model families
Rollout plan documented with canary thresholds and fallback to existing arbitration policy
Design doc reviewed by runtime and infra (two approvals) and a small-scale experiment run with clear dashboards
implementation_notes: Introduce PhaseGroup abstraction: tag requests as PREFILL_DOMINANT or DECODE_DOMINANT using lightweight prefix heuristics (token count, prompt markers)
Time-sliced phase windows: default 20ms decode window / 50ms prefill window (experimentable via config)
Per-window soft cap: allow burst up to 1.5x then proportional backoff to maintain fairness
Kernel hint propagation: scheduler annotates batched work with kernel_preference (fast-decode | memory-efficient-prefill)
KV cache policy: avoid evicting prefill KV entries during decode windows; implement read-priority vs write-priority rules
Interaction with batching: decode windows favor small immediate batches; prefill windows allow larger aggregated batches for throughput
Fallback: if phase identification confidence < 0.6, fall back to hybrid arbitration to avoid misclassification impact
Metrics to emit: per-phase P50/P95/P99 latency, phase throughput (tokens/s), starvation_count, kernel_switch_count, avg_batch_size
test_plan: Unit tests for PhaseGroup classification with edge cases (short prompt followed by long decode, streaming prefill)
Integration test: end-to-end with synthetic workload generator (configurable mix of prefill/decode lengths)
Perf harness runs against small (124M), medium (1.3B), and large (13B) models to capture kernel-selection interactions
Chaos test: random misclassification injection to ensure graceful fallback and no correctness violation
A/B canary on a subset of production traffic (5% -> 20%) with automatic rollback on SLO breach
rollout_plan: Stage 0: local simulation/synthetic runs (incubation) - map param space for phase window sizes
Stage 1: dev cluster canary with non-production traffic, run 48h, validate metrics
Stage 2: production canary 5% traffic, observe 72h with strict rollback thresholds: decode P99 must not regress >5% and starvation_count must drop
Stage 3: ramp to 20% then to 50% if criteria pass, full rollout only after performance and reliability sign-off
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Misclassification could penalize mixed requests (both heavy prefill + decode). Mitigation: confidence threshold and hybrid fallback.
Risk: Increased kernel switching frequency causing overhead. Mitigation: batch kernel hints and limit switch rate per-GPU per-second.
Risk: KV cache thrash when prefill windows are short. Mitigation: conservative prefill window defaults and read-priority rules.
Risk: Regression for encoder-decoder models where prefill semantics differ. Mitigation: model-family aware rules and opt-out flags
